script: I ran my fanfic through a university AI and got stunned.. I was on my laptop, scrolling through the final draft of my fanfic—yeah, the one where I turned my crush into a dragon for the ultimate plot twist—when I hit the "Upload to Proofreader" button. I thought, "Bruh, this is just a spellcheck, no big deal." The program was advertised as a combo of Grammarly and Claude, so I assumed it'd just catch typos. But when I hit submit, the screen flashed an error: "Copyright violation detected. RPF content not allowed." I stared. I'd written a fanfic, not a copyrighted script. I thought, "Maybe it's a glitch." So I renamed the file, swapped out all the character names for generic ones like Perro, Conejito, and Oso, hoping to dodge whatever algorithm was chewing on my text. The next thing I saw was a wall of text warning me about "purposely attempting to bypass administrative laws." Then the app crashed. I was left staring at a blue screen. The next morning, the dean's office called. "Your account was flagged for violating the acceptable internet usage policy. We're opening a manual review." My heart dropped. I didn't even know the proofreader was actually running Claude under the hood. I had no idea it could read the content at all. I am in university, juggling classes, and now my fanfic is sitting on a dean's desk. I didn't even submit it to anyone; I just wanted a spellcheck. I am basically the poster child for how overzealous AI can turn a harmless hobby into a campus scandal. So yeah, I used a school‑approved proofreader to scan an RPF fanfic, the AI's guardrails are tighter than a pop‑up ad blocker, and now my school has to read my story. The audacity. (I know, right?)
